summary.intent: Fix a failing Phala TEE deployment caused by an invalid Docker image reference with an uppercase repository owner, while keeping the repo owner variable-driven for future org migration.
summary.outcome: Identified that `envsubst` does not support bash `:-default` syntax, causing the image reference to resolve incorrectly. Fixed `docker-compose.phala.yml` to use plain `${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER}` without the default fallback, committed on a fix branch.

repo: The CI workflow (`deploy-staging.yml`) lowercases `GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER` before calling `envsubst`, so plain `${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER}` in compose files resolves correctly to lowercase.
Phala's `phala deploy` receives the `envsubst`-processed file from `/tmp/docker-compose.phala.yml`, not the original — but the substitution was broken due to the `:-OWNER` default syntax.
The project is `FSM1/cipher-box` on GitHub (owner `fsm1` lowercase); GHCR requires all-lowercase image references.

Phase 36 (inline upload progress) was recently merged to main: replaced `UploadItem.tsx` + `UploadModal.tsx` with `UploadListItem.tsx`, refactored `upload.store.ts` and `useDropUpload.ts`, deleted `useFileUpload.ts` and `upload.service.ts`.

code.finding: Changed `ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER:-OWNER}/cipherbox-tee-worker:${TAG:-latest}` to `ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER}/cipherbox-tee-worker:${TAG:-latest}`. `envsubst` (GNU gettext) does not parse bash `:-default` syntax — it either treats the whole expression as an unknown variable name or produces a broken substitution.

Workflow runs `envsubst` on the compose file into `/tmp/docker-compose.phala.yml` and passes that to `phala deploy`. `GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER` is already lowercased in the CI environment before this step.

workflow: `envsubst` (GNU gettext) does not support bash parameter expansion defaults (`${VAR:-default}`). Using such syntax in files processed by `envsubst` produces broken output — strip defaults and ensure the variable is always set upstream.
Worktree cleanup is a manual step after CI/agent work; stale worktrees from CI debug sessions persist until explicitly removed.

friction: `envsubst` silently produced a broken image reference rather than erroring — the bug only surfaced at Phala deploy time, not in CI.
The `:-OWNER` default in the compose file was misleading: it implied a safe fallback but actually caused the failure.
open_items: Verify the fix branch CI run succeeds end-to-end on the Phala staging deploy before merging.
Consider auditing other compose files or CI templates for `${VAR:-default}` patterns passed through `envsubst`.
